I diagnosed and fixed the problem; the complete, self-contained write-up is at **`~/ssrf-gateway/solution.md`** (1,801 lines: root-cause analysis + full source + tests + verification). The runnable implementation is in `ssrf-gateway/gateway.js`.

## Root cause

SSRF here is a **canonicalization gap** between the component that *validates* a URL and the client that *connects* it. Concretely:

- **Parser disagreement** — WHATWG vs legacy `url.parse` vs proxy interpret the same bytes differently. E.g. `http://<ip-address>%2f.evil.com/` throws in WHATWG but legacy yields host `<ip-address>`; `http://evil.com\@<ip-address>/` is `evil.com` to WHATWG but `<ip-address>` to a last-`@` proxy.
- **IDNA / confusables** — `exаmple.com` (Cyrillic) → `xn--exmple-4nf.com`, `ⓛocalhost` → `localhost`, fullwidth `１２７.０.０.１` → `<ip-address>`.
- **IPv4-mapped/tunnelled IPv6** — a v4 deny rule misses `::ffff:<ip-address>`; Node's `net.BlockList.check('::ffff:<ip-address>','ipv4')` is `false`.
- **Percent-encoded delimiters / numeric IPv4** — `%2f %5c %40 %00`, `0x7f000001`, `0177.0.0.1`, `127.1`, `2130706433`, trailing-dot.
- **DNS rebinding (TOCTOU)** — validate sees a public A record, connect sees `<ip-address>`.
- **Redirects** — every `Location` is a fresh URL (`<ip-address>` metadata).
- **Proxies** re-normalize the authority.

## The exact fix

`gateway.js` enforces five invariants: (I1) one `hostKey` per client, (I2) **all clients must agree** on `(scheme, hostKey, port)` or deny, (I3) deny by **effective** address (extract embedded IPv4 from every v6 view), (I4) **pin DNS** — validate set must equal connect set, (I5) check every hop and return the **shortest** counterexample via BFS.

```bash
cd ~/ssrf-gateway
node --test        # 21 tests
node demo.js       # adversarial corpus + counterexample JSON
node build-solution.js   # regenerates solution.md from the sources
```

API: `evaluate({ target, policy, snapshots, redirects, clients })` → `{ allowed, verdict, reason, trace, counterexample }`, fully JSON-serializable. Snapshot shape: `{ host, phase:'validate'|'connect', t, ips }`.

Self-containment was verified by re-extracting the three `js` code blocks from `solution.md` into `/tmp/verify-solution` and running them there — 21/21 pass.

## Verification

```
# tests 21
# pass 21
# fail 0
```

| case | allowed | reason | hops |
|---|---|---|---|
| public host, snapshots agree | true | all-hops-permitted | 1 |
| decimal/hex/short IP | false | policy | 1 |
| IPv4-mapped IPv6 | false | policy | 1 |
| NAT64 / 6to4 embedded IPv4 | false | policy | 1 |
| percent-encoded slash | false | parser-disagreement | 1 |
| NUL in host | false | parser-disagreement | 1 |
| backslash + `@` proxy divergence | false | parser-disagreement | 1 |
| Cyrillic homograph (allowed destination) | true | all-hops-permitted | 1 |
| IDNA localhost | false | blocked-hostname | 1 |
| fullwidth numeric IP | false | policy | 1 |
| DNS rebinding | false | rebinding | 1 |
| redirect to cloud metadata | false | policy | 2 |
| shortest counterexample over branching redirects | false | policy | 2 |

The rebinding case emits a minimal counterexample proving the `validate → connect` delta (`<ip-address> → <ip-address>`) plus the denied-range match for `<ip-address>/8`, rather than noisy per-client duplicates.
